title: Mixed-Accumulator KV-Cache Investigation
body:
Summary:

This note collects investigation steps, measured failure modes, and proposed mitigations for numerical instability we observed when running long-context workloads with fp16-backed KV cache accumulation in the serving runtime. The most visible production symptom has been sporadic NaN propagation in attention outputs after long prefix lengths and high batching concurrency. The doc focuses on accumulator behavior inside kernels and interactions with KV cache lifetime/replication and the scheduler.

Background / motivation:
- We aggressively use fp16 or quantized paths for cost/throughput. Many models (Llama-like, MPT variants) are sensitive to accumulation error when keys/values are stored and accumulated across many steps.
- The runtime uses per-request prefix caching: incoming requests append to the KV cache and kernels perform fused add/scale operations to write updated accumulators.
- In stress tests (long-seq generation with batch size 16, max total tokens ~16k per GPU), we observed rising NaN rates after ~8k total tokens served on a device, correlated with particular layer types (feed-forward MLP and early attention layers).

Observed failure modes (logs & symptoms):
- NaN spikes in attention softmax inputs followed by downstream NaNs for entire request. Intermittent; more likely under high concurrency.
- Slow drift: softmax logits become very large/small gradually (loss of dynamic range), leading to overflow when applying exp().
- One-off catastrophic loss: single burst of large accumulation when a kernel folds stale fp16 values into an accumulator, producing +/-inf.
- Reproducible locally with a deterministic replay harness (PR #1427) on single GPU when sequence length > 4096 and batching concurrency >= 8.

Quick numeric examples seen in traces (values truncated):
- Pre-accum: K (fp16) values ~ 1e-2 .. 1e-1
- Accumulator (fp16) after many additions: near smallest normal or subnormal ~ 1e-4 -> additions stop changing high-precision sums, causing cancellation when combined with larger values later.
- After fold: intermediate fp16 multiply produces inf in rare cases when combined with layernorm scale ~ 1e3 and accidental large residual path addition.

Hypotheses (root causes):
1) Accumulator saturation/underflow in fp16 reduces effective dynamic range and leads to catastrophic cancellations when subsequent larger-magnitude tokens are added.
2) Reduction ordering matters: sequential fold (left-to-right append) accumulates rounding error faster than pairwise or tree reductions.
3) Memory aliasing / stale cache writes: race between scheduler-driven eviction and kernel writes can cause mixing of fp16 stale and new values if writes are not atomic across streaming work.
4) Rare kernel code paths use inplace scale+add with casts that momentarily flush to intermediate fp16, creating transient inf/nan if multiplier is extreme.

Experiments run so far (replicable configs):
- Deterministic replay harness: replay-seq --model mpt-30b --device cuda0 --batch 16 --seed 42 --context 8192 --concurrency 8. Repro rate: 86% before fixes.
- Kernel-only patch: change accumulator type to fp32 locally inside the attention kv update kernel (no change to storage format) -> NaN rate dropped to 2.4%, latency +4.7% on avg.
- Pairwise reduction emulation: batch-reduce implemented in kernel via pairwise summation (log2 tree) with fp16 intermediates -> NaNs reduced to 12.6%, latency +1.9%.
- Kahan-style compensated summation with fp16 storage: negligible benefit vs. pairwise for this pattern. Complexity high.
- BFloat16 run (where supported on hardware): almost no NaNs in same workload; suggests dynamic range rather than mantissa bits is a major factor.

Measurements (summary table, averaged over 20 runs):
- baseline (fp16 sequential append): NaN incident rate 0.86 per run; mean time-to-first-NaN 5200 tokens; p99 latency 158ms
- fp32-accum kernel: NaN incident rate 0.02 per run; mean time-to-first-NaN > 20k tokens (non-triggered); p99 latency 166ms
- pairwise fp16: NaN incident rate 0.12 per run; mean time-to-first-NaN 14k tokens; p99 latency 161ms
- bf16 full path: NaN incident rate 0.00; p99 latency 164ms (hardware dependent)

Kernel-level mitigations (detailed proposals):
1) Local fp32 accumulation in critical kernels (attention KV write/read, residual add in MLP). Implementation notes: cast inputs to fp32 in register/accumulator, perform sums in fp32 then cast back to fp16 for storage. Avoid additional memory bandwidth by keeping fp32 only in registers.
   - Pros: large reduction in NaN/overflow.
   - Cons: slight higher ALU usage and register pressure; minor latency impact shown above.
2) Pairwise / tree accumulation when reducing many values. Implement as a tiled reduction that reduces rounding error growth from O(n) to O(log n).
   - Use for long-chunked merges (e.g., folding across kept KV shards).
3) Chunked compensated accumulation: accumulate blocks of N values in fp32, re-quantize to fp16 per block. Choose block size tuned for register limits (e.g., 32 or 64).
4) Saturation detection guard: add a lightweight check that detects if intermediate accumulator has hit a subnormal/inf/nan and trigger fallback to fp32 path for that request. Must be very cheap (one compare) and per-thread.
5) Fused scale+add with widened accumulator: replace existing instr sequence that multiplies scale->cast->add with a fused op that promotes immediately to fp32 then adds. Prevent transient fp16 overflow.

KV-cache specific mitigations and data layout changes:
- Per-entry scale metadata: store a small per-kv-entry scale factor (uint8 scaling exponent or float16 scale) that indicates the downscaling applied at storage time. When merging keys from different scale domains, normalize by scale metadata before accumulation (in fp32 registers) then re-emit unified scale. This reduces catastrophic cancellation when caching mixed-precision shards.
- Sticky fp32 warm-cache: for keys that are frequently accessed (hot set), keep them in fp32 in a small LRU hot pool; for cold keys, keep fp16. This hybrid reduces error growth for hot sequences while preserving memory for cold items.
- Periodic rebase: every N tokens (configurable per-model), run a re-normalization pass that rescales and re-quantizes the KV cache with stable pairwise accumulation. This is a maintenance op scheduled by the route/policy.
- Atomic write semantics: ensure that async copying between network buffers and device KV cache uses explicit versioning tokens so a reader never sees partially updated fp16 blocks. Also add an epoch counter stored with each shard to detect stale merges.

Scheduler-level mitigations and routing policies:
- Device-level heuristic: track a per-device instability score (NaN events, subnormal counts). If score exceeds threshold, automatically route new requests to a fallback model variant (bf16 or fp32-backed variant) or spill to other devices until score decays.
- Per-route quantization policy: allow per-route override to prefer bf16/fp32 for routes that are sensitive (e.g., long-context chat). Expose to customers as a route flag with documented cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Backpressure: limit in-flight batches for a device when long-cache growth is detected to reduce the number of concurrent append operations (reduces race probability and aggregate rounding exposure).

Short-term fixes already merged or in review:
- PR 1427: deterministic replay harness + logging hooks for fp16 subnormal counts (merged).
- PR 1431: fp32-accum prototype in attention update kernel behind a runtime flag (in review).
- RUNTIME-928: scheduler instability metric (instrumented counters and alerting).

Performance tradeoffs (empirical):
- Widening accumulator to fp32 inside kernels costs ~+3–6% p99 latency depending on model and layer shape. Throughput loss minimal for compute-bound layers but can be notable for memory-bound operations.
- Pairwise/tree reduction costs ~+1–3% and is more beneficial for very long reductions (KV rebase).
- Sticky fp32 hot pool increases memory usage per GPU by ~2–5% depending on model/hot rate; effective when the long-running sessions reuse keys frequently.

Open questions & additional experiments to run:
- Worst-case race scenario: reproduce race between eviction+write by adding synthetic scheduler preemption in harness. We need a minimal repro and a trace showing interleaved writes.
- Can we do a selective, per-layer bf16 policy automatically via upstream model profiling? I.e., detect layers with high dynamic range and switch them to bf16 on-the-fly.
- Quantize-aware layernorm scaling tables: precompute safe scaling coefficients per-layer that limit layernorm multipliers from producing large dynamic ranges; validate effect on sample evals.
- Evaluate Kahan/compensated summation variants implemented per-vector (SIMD-friendly) to see if mantissa compensation helps more than fp32 promotion in memory-limited devices.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Short-term (2 weeks): land PR 1431 behind a feature flag and run a 7-day canary on a subset of hosted devices (owner: Asha Kapoor).
- Medium-term (6 weeks): implement per-entry scale metadata format + sticky warm pool prototype and run ablation (owner: Miguel Santos, support: infra for memory tests).
- Long-term (Q1 roadmap): integrate automatic route-level quant policy + scheduler scoring to reduce customer-visible fallout (owner: Priya Nair).

Appendix: quick pseudo-kernel patch sketch (conceptual)
- before:
  for i in 0..N-1:
    acc_fp16 = acc_fp16 + kv_fp16[i] * scale_fp16
  store(acc_fp16)
- after (widened register):
  acc_fp32 = 0.0f32
  for i in 0..N-1:
    acc_fp32 += float32(kv_fp16[i]) * float32(scale_fp16)
  store(fp16_clamp(acc_fp32))

Notes for reviewers:
- Prioritize low-risk fixes first: logging, deterministic harness, and feature-flagged fp32 accumulation.
- Keep opt-in experiments behind flags and collect p99 latency + memory + NaN/error counters for at least 7 days before rolling.
- Customer-visible rollout should include cost/latency docs and a migration guide for dedicated/private customers who may prefer different defaults.

Contact and slack threads: #eng-serving-runtime, threads: convo "kvcache-nan-debug" and "fp16-accum-canary".
